governance.anchor: Is G_t actually an independent KnowledgeOS state variable, or merely a derived quality measure? ... Does the kernel itself have a formally definable "transcendence" operation

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: No formally tagged lineage_claims row connects a to b by label name (a's own tags target other artifacts: 'kernel always busy...' statement and its own extension by S2252); basis kept INFERRED rather than CORROBORATED on that account, though the content-level redefinition is well-evidenced.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: b (S2231/S2232) formalizes guna as a continuous regime vector G_t=(s_t,r_t,m_t) in the simplex Delta^2, embedded in E_t=(K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,N_t), explicitly leaving open 'Is G_t actually an independent KnowledgeOS state variable, or merely a derived quality measure?' -- i.e. treating guna as a possible fourth Sigma-adjacent dimension. a (S2247/S2248) directly reformulates this: 'Central hypothesis: Guna mode is NOT another knowledge dimension (i.e. not a sixth axis of Sigma); rather Guna mode = a control/state variable governing how the kernel operates on knowledge', replacing b's continuous Delta^2-valued regime with a discrete M_t in {S,R,T} that gates admissible kernel operators (O_S/O_R/O_T subset O). The group's own why_grouped note confirms this directly: a 'Explicitly distinguishes this from the earlier per-chapter guna-conditioning-regime object [b] by treating mode as a control variable rather than a fourth Sigma dimension.' Both concern the same underlying Sattva/Rajas/Tamas subject matter but formalize it with incompatible type shapes (continuous simplex-valued regime vector vs. discrete control-variable enum).
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a's mode-as-control-variable formalization were developed with no awareness of or reference to b's earlier regime-vector treatment (pure independent invention rather than a deliberate reformulation), this would be better read as INDEPENDENT parallel work on the same theme rather than a REDEFINITION of b -- though the explicit 'distinguishes this from the earlier...object' framing in the group note argues against that.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Both fully shown (no truncation); a is a 91-source-id spanning registry (S2224-S2302) of which only chapter-14-relevant entries connect to b -- the relationship is between a's general scheme and b as one of its many chapter-specific inputs.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: a is the running T0-T4 tier scheme and C1-C20 negative-constraint registry tracked across all 18 Gita chapters (S2224...S2302). b is specifically Chapter 14's Guna/conditioning-regime reading (S2231/S2232: Sattva/Rajas/Tamas, Moksha-as-transcendence-of-conditioning-regime). a's own running-tally rows show the registry being directly extended with Chapter-14-specific content, e.g. S2251 'Records two new T0s: equal treatment of evidence (refuted per above) and Cha[pter 14 mapping refused]' -- a's general classification scheme is extended with b's chapter-specific findings as new registry entries.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If the truncated 'Cha[pter 14...]' reference in S2251 actually refers to a different chapter or a different claim not from this specific b family, the direct extension link would be weaker than claimed.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Explicit POSSIBLY-RELATION note (G0496): B 'Combines Gita Chapter 13 (Kshetra/Kshetrajna ontology)... with Chapter 14 (Guna conditioning)... into a two-layer research model E_t=(K_t,C_t)' -- B explicitly extends A's Chapter-14-only guna/conditioning theory (G_t=(s_t,r_t,m_t)) by composing it with the separate Chapter-13 field/knower ontology.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If C_t in B is shown to be mathematically identical to A's G_t rather than a deliberately distinct, renamed variable (the note states C_t is 'deliberately not called guna'), this could shift toward REDEFINITION instead of EXTENSION.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Tamas \rightarrow poor discrimination \rightarrow bad operation \rightarrow worse knowledge state \rightarrow more Tamas
rationale_evidence.statement: Interprets 'without governance mind can become its own enemy' via a self-reinforcing epistemic degradation feedback loop: G_t -> B_t (Buddhi) -> o_t (chosen operation) -> K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t) -> G_{t+1}, with worked examples Tamas->poor discrimination->bad operation->worse knowledge state->more Tamas, and Rajas->excessive activity->attachment to outcomes->more activity->more Rajas. Proposed as a possible mathematical model of self-reinforcing epistemic degradation, a candidate KnowledgeOS research direction.

# hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory

**Scope(s):** THEORY-LEVEL · **Row count:** 8 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** ACTIVE · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** E_t=(K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,N_t), G_t=(s_t,r_t,m_t) in Delta^2, K_t=(C_t,Sigma_t,Q_t) · **Aliases:** Chapter 14 Three Modes of Material Nature reading, Guna-atita transcendence hypothesis
**Candidate group membership (NOT an identity claim):**
- G0495: [`gita-kernel-candidate-tier-scheme-T0-T4` · `hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory' POSSIBLY relates to 'gita-kernel-candidate-tier-scheme-T0-T4' (batch B0054). Note: Disciplined hpa reading of Gita Chapter 14 (Sattva/Rajas/Tamas) treating the gunas as a dynamic CONDITIONING REGIME of the epistemic process (candidate kernel operating condition, explicitly refused as a kernel primitive), not a Sigma-axis value substitution (contrast with artifact-19's E2 finding against the external_research Ch14 formalization). Introduces Knowledge existence != Knowledge availability (Tamas covers knowledge without removing it), Knowledge Quality != Epistemic Freedom (Sattva can bind through attachment to knowledge), a self-reinforcing epistemic degradation feedback loop (G_t->B_t->o_t->K_{t+1}->G_{t+1}), and a three-layer distinction Knowledge != Knowledge Quality != Epistemic Freedom, feeding a revised Moksha hypothesis (transcendence of the conditioning regime, G_t->G_perp, not max(K) or max(Sattva)).
- G0496: [`hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory` · `hpa-gita-chapters13-14-composed-field-condition-model`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapters13-14-composed-field-condition-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory' (batch B0054). Note: Combines Gita Chapter 13 (Kshetra/Kshetrajna ontology: what the field/knower are) with Chapter 14 (Guna conditioning: under what condition the field is processed) into a two-layer research model E_t=(K_t,C_t) where C_t is epistemic conditioning state (deliberately not called guna in the canonical model). Poses three hypotheses about G_t's status: (A) derived from Sigma, (B) an independent state variable alongside Sigma, (C) a property of the kernel's operating condition rather than of the knowledge state -- favors (C). Distinguishes four failure modes previously conflated as bad knowledge (false proposition; true proposition + failure to recognize significance; true proposition + inappropriate attachment; true proposition + insufficient discrimination), warns explicitly against Sattva=correct/Rajas=incorrect/Tamas=false oversimplification, and gives final candidate model (K_t,G_t) -Buddhi(B_t)-> o_t -delta-> K_{t+1}, explicitly marked GITA-13/14 RESEARCH HYPOTHESIS, NOT CANONICAL.
- G0508: [`gita-guna-mode-conditioned-state-machine-hypothesis` · `hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'gita-guna-mode-conditioned-state-machine-hypothesis' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory' (batch B0054). Note: Reformulates guna (Sattva/Rajas/Tamas) explicitly as a MODE/STATE model (not Gita metaphysics): K_t=(X_t,M_t) with M_t in {S,R,T} a control/state variable governing which kernel operators are admissible (O_S, O_R, O_T subset O), rather than a fourth Sigma dimension. Gives mode-specific operator sets (O_S={Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate}; O_R={Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute}; O_T={DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence}), a mode-sensitive Buddhi discriminator B_t:(E_t,K_t,M_t)->{accept,reject,investigate,suspend,transform} (same evidence yields different actions per mode), and a Tamas->Zero->Buddhi->Sattva mode-transition hypothesis. Explicitly distinguishes this from the earlier per-chapter guna-conditioning-regime object by treating mode as a control variable rather than a fourth Sigma dimension, and poses a 10-question research checklist (can S/R/T be defined without theology, can modes be detected computationally, is mode another axis or a control variable over axes, etc).
- G0523: [`gita-guna-mode-conditioned-state-machine-hypothesis` · `hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory`] — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'gita-guna-mode-conditioned-state-machine-hypothesis' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter14-guna-conditioning-regime-theory' (batch B0055). Note: The Guna-as-kernel-operating-mode hypothesis, first proposed in B0054 and substantially extended in B0055 (mode-dependent Buddhi, an independent mode state machine, later reframed as a falsifiable experimental control variable).

## Rationale
Interprets 'without governance mind can become its own enemy' via a self-reinforcing epistemic degradation feedback loop: G_t -> B_t (Buddhi) -> o_t (chosen operation) -> K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t) -> G_{t+1}, with worked examples Tamas->poor discrimination->bad operation->worse knowledge state->more Tamas, and Rajas->excessive activity->attachment to outcomes->more activity->more Rajas. Proposed as a possible mathematical model of self-reinforcing epistemic degradation, a candidate KnowledgeOS research direction [S2231].
